_meta.description: Sector taxonomy for transition risk layer. Aggregated from GICS industries, NACE Rev. 2, and EXIOBASE-3 sector list. Each sector keys into pass-through, learning-curve, IO matrix and CCExposure tables.
sources: EXIOBASE-3 sector list (Stadler et al. 2018, https://doi.org/10.1111/jiec.12715)

field_notes.emission_intensity_t_per_revenue: DIRECT (Scope-1) emission intensity, tCO2 per MILLION USD of sector GROSS OUTPUT (EEIO/EXIOBASE-3-informed sector averages). Used ONLY by Layer 3 to build the sector-typical carbon price shock (fraction of output = EI x 1e-6 x carbon_price x pass_through), which is clamped to <=1.0 for the linear propagation basis. Fossil sectors are O(1000s); services O(10s). Screening approximation.
field_notes.io_index: Position in the io_matrix.json A matrix (0-indexed, must match _meta.sector_order).
field_notes.stranding_slope: R7 — per-sector logistic stranding slope (default 0.20 if absent). Higher = faster impairment diffusion once the L2 crossover triggers, calibrated to asset turnover speed.
field_notes.intermediate_input_share: Share of output that is bought-in intermediate inputs (1 − value-added). Layer 3 indirect upstream-carbon cost scales by revenue × this share, so labour/margin-heavy sectors (services, finance, real estate) don't book an implausibly large supply-chain carbon cost. EXIOBASE / national-accounts informed. Default 0.5 if absent.
field_notes.io_proxy: For sectors added after the 20-sector I-O matrix was built, io_proxy names the existing matrix row used for Layer-3 propagation. All other params (emission intensity, pass-through, CCExposure, pathway, tech pair) are the sector's own. Lets us resolve the BSR lever-library sectors without rebuilding the 20x20/980x980 matrices.

power_coal.label: Electric Power — Coal
power_coal.notes: Highest stranding risk under fast-transition scenarios; near-zero learning rate.

power_gas.label: Electric Power — Natural Gas
power_gas.notes: Stranding risk highest for new-build peakers as battery costs decline.

power_renewable.label: Electric Power — Renewables
power_renewable.notes: Beneficiary of transition; revenue uplift in fast-transition scenarios.

oil_upstream.label: Oil & Gas — Upstream
oil_upstream.notes: Demand collapse in NZ2050; reserves stranding from Carbon Tracker (2022).

steel.label: Steel & Iron
steel.notes: Trade-exposed; low pass-through (~30%) per Fabra & Reguant 2014.

cement.label: Cement & Lime
cement.notes: Process emissions ~60% of total; CCUS dependency for net-zero alignment.

aluminium.label: Aluminium & Non-Ferrous Metals
aluminium.notes: Highly Scope 2 dependent; benefits from grid decarbonisation.

road_transport_ice.label: Automotive — Internal Combustion
road_transport_ice.notes: Demand collapse 2030-2040 in NZ scenarios; capex pivot required.

road_transport_ev.label: Automotive — Electric Vehicles
road_transport_ev.notes: Beneficiary; battery cost declines drive demand.

aviation.label: Aviation (Passenger & Freight)
aviation.notes: Limited substitutes; high transition cost without SAF scale.

real_estate_commercial.label: Real Estate — Commercial
real_estate_commercial.notes: EU EPBD / NYC LL97 / UK MEES drive retrofit costs.

real_estate_residential.label: Real Estate — Residential
real_estate_residential.notes: Slower regulatory pace than commercial; long replacement cycles.

data_center.label: Data Centres
data_center.notes: Scope 2 dominant; PPA strategy changes risk profile.

services.label: Services & Other
services.notes: Low-intensity; minimal direct transition cost; supply-chain pass-through dominates.

consumer_goods.label: Consumer Goods (FMCG)
consumer_goods.notes: Branded FMCG; Scope-3-heavy supply chains; some pricing power.

financial_services.label: Financial Services
financial_services.notes: Own-operations emissions tiny; financed-emissions / regulatory exposure dominates (not modelled here).

healthcare.label: Healthcare & Pharma
healthcare.notes: Energy-intensive facilities + medical supply chain; demand grows.

professional_services.label: Professional Services
professional_services.notes: Advisory/consulting; office energy + travel; minimal direct transition cost.

telecom.label: Telecommunications
telecom.notes: Network energy Scope-2 dominant; PPA strategy changes profile (like data centres).

metals_mining.label: Metals & Mining (transition minerals)
metals_mining.notes: Copper/lithium/nickel etc. — a transition BENEFICIARY: demand GROWS. High Scope-1 (diesel/processing) but no product-demand stranding.

industrial_equipment.label: Industrial & Construction Equipment
industrial_equipment.notes: Own-ops emissions modest; the transition risk is the USE-PHASE of sold products (diesel engines/machinery). Customers face carbon costs and electrify — demand/margin pressure on the maker. Slower than autos (duty cycles, charging in the field).

pulp_paper.label: Pulp & Paper
pulp_paper.notes: Energy-intensive but largely BIOMASS-powered (black liquor / hog fuel) — low FOSSIL Scope 1; residual fossil in lime kilns + purchased power carries the carbon-compliance cost. Not a stranding risk (no cheaper substitute obsoletes pulp). A low-carbon producer with green-power-sales and biogenic-carbon optionality (opportunity tilt in L4). EU mills face EU ETS; N. American mills a lower carbon backstop.

wood_products_timber.label: Solid Wood & Mass Timber
wood_products_timber.notes: Sawmilling / engineered wood / MASS TIMBER — a transition BENEFICIARY: mass timber displaces steel & cement in construction, so demand GROWS as those sectors decarbonise. Low-energy, carbon-STORING product. No product-demand stranding; strong opportunity tilt in L4.
